text:
olivia: Customer reported a 413 from /v1/rerank. They say it happens intermittently when they send large doc sets, and the error message is just "payload too large" with no guidance. Can we triage? :thinking_face:

matt_s: Do we have the exact request body or at least counts? docs count + avg doc size + query length?

olivia: Pasted the minimal repro the customer sent (they sanitized PII):
```
POST /v1/rerank
{
  "query": "Best troubleshooting steps for router outages...",
  "documents": [ /* 1,150 docs, each ~1.2k characters avg */ ],
  "metadata": {"customer_id": "redacted"}
}
```
Customer says they start seeing 413 once total characters > ~1.3M or so. They also attached our 413 response body: "Payload too large" (no details).

devon: That matches a token-ceiling hit. Our rerank path enforces a conservative request token cap (server-side) to protect memory/latency. The UX currently bubbles the HTTP 413 but doesn't include the configured token cap or next steps.

jordan_p: Steps to repro locally: 1) craft a JSON with many small docs until request size > 1MB, 2) curl to /v1/rerank with API key, 3) check X-Request-Id and server logs. If they can share X-Request-Id we can confirm in logs.

olivia: Customer doesn't want to share logs; asked for clear instructions they can follow. They also reported inconsistent ranking when they manually truncate docs vs when server rejects the request. They want: exact limits, deterministic guidance (chunking rules), and a nicer error message they can depend on.

matt_s: Proposed support reply: short + actionable. Example: "Your request exceeded the rerank input limit (max ~200k tokens). Please reduce number of docs or size per doc, or break into multiple requests and re-aggregate results. If you share X-Request-Id we can confirm which limit triggered the rejection." We should verify the actual numeric limit before sending.

devon: Confirming: current enforcement checks estimated tokens (query + sum(docs)) and falls back at ~200k tokens for the hosted tier. For Dedicated customers that can be higher depending on plan. I'll confirm exact value and whether chars vs tokens was used in the rejection logic.

ashley_cs: Can we add a short FAQ snippet for support replies and an example chunking pattern? Eg: send docs in batches of 200, re-rank per-batch, then do a final merge step on top-k from each batch. Keep examples minimal.

supportbot: Incident note created: INC-2026-045 - rerank 413 UX. Assigned to devon. :white_check_mark:

jordan_p: Triage checklist for devs: 1) confirm server-side limit and exact metric (bytes vs tokens). 2) update 413 payload to include friendly fields: {"error":"payload_too_large", "limit_type": "tokens", "limit_value": "200000", "suggested_action": "chunk docs into batches of N or use streaming/rerank-batching" } 3) surface Dedicated overrides in response if applicable. 4) add KB article for chunking patterns.

olivia: Customer-facing reply draft (short): "Thanks — this is a token/size limit on the rerank endpoint. We recommend batching your docs (example pattern attached) or sending only candidate passages to rerank. If you can share the X-Request-Id from the failing request we can confirm which limit was hit and advise next steps."

ashley_cs: I'll send that after devon confirms the numeric limit. Also adding a snippet for them to compute an estimate: 
```
// rough token estimate for UTF-8 text
approx_tokens = Math.ceil(chars / 4.0)
// target per-request tokens < 200000
```

devon: I'm going to: (a) verify exact limit and if it's per-request or per-model, (b) add the more detailed 413 payload with limit info, and (c) create a KB draft. Will update thread when done.

olivia: Thanks everyone — keeping customer updated. :pray:
